title: Conformance report (mverify)
description: The structured shape a /mverify conformance shard (one per module/repo) returns, and the aggregate the skill assembles. Change-shaped: findings mirror a change doc's Affected Code Paths rows so gaps feed straight into an mspec/mreverse follow-up. Detection only — never rewrites.

change_ref.description: The change/plan/spec unit this shard was checked against.

shard.description: Names which sweep produced the report — the kind axis (scope.kind is the granularity axis). cross-repo occurs on both axes with different meanings: as scope.kind it means the report covers a boundary rather than one repo; as shard it names the sweep that compares producers against consumers. Required unless scope.kind is aggregate.

clean.description: true iff findings is empty for this scope; on the aggregate it means no shard reported a finding.

type.description: missing/extra/mismatch = change<->code surface drift; coupling = cross-module IMPLEMENTATION import or cross-repo ref bypassing context/shared/spec/; cross-repo-drift = a producer/consumer that doesn't match the frozen shared contract; stale-contract-revision = delivered code that conforms to the agreement revision it was built against and to no other. The last is deliberately its own type rather than a cross-repo-drift, because the remedy differs — drift means somebody diverged from the contract, whereas this means the contract moved underneath conforming work, and only the latter is scheduled as remediation rather than investigated as a mistake.

spec_ref.description: Spec/contract surface the code was checked against (file + signature/type).

code_path.description: Source path (relative to repos/<repo>/) where the drift/violation lives.

built_against.description: On a stale-contract-revision finding: the agreement revision the delivered code was built against.

current_revision.description: On a stale-contract-revision finding: the revision the agreement now carries. Together with built_against this makes the gap legible without re-deriving it.
